title: Owner withdrawing the revoked OLD minter's USDe position via withdrawAsOwner while the market strategy is below par makes StableStakerV2 absorb the entire commingled loss (first-exiter-paid-in-full ordering reverses the minter cushion)
relatedSites: AYieldStrategy.sol:732-755 (_withdrawInternal debits requested amount); ERC4626MarketYieldStrategy.sol:158-180 (_disposeShares sells convertToShares(amount), the NAV-equivalent of the debited principal)
description: The market strategy pays an exiter the NAV of the principal debited: _withdrawInternal (AYieldStrategy.sol:732-755) passes the requested (capped) amount to _disposeShares, which sells vault.convertToShares(amount) (ERC4626MarketYieldStrategy.sol:160). When the commingled position is below par (V < D), the FIRST exiter is therefore made whole and the LAST exiters bear the entire loss (I4 dominance, held at all 589 run-18 cap-binds). On the live USDe strategy 0xaC2e…7f95 the clients are: OLD PhusdStableMinter 0x435B…77E5 3,749.62 USDe (revoked minter, ~58% of D = 6,477.66), StableStakerV2 0xA6d3…B58F 2,684.40, new minter 0x9485…E60C 43.65, V1 0. The minter-cushion design intends the non-redeeming minter to share (cushion) V2's loss. If the owner retires the revoked OLD minter by calling withdrawAsOwner(0x435B, recipient, 3,749.62e18) while V < D, the minter is paid in full and V2 — the only redeeming client — absorbs the whole realised loss; V2 then emits Antimatter against under-backed principal (dilution). A competent owner tidying up a revoked minter would not expect exit ORDER to decide who bears the loss.
notCommingledCap: This is EXIT-ORDERING, not the commingled share cap. The minter-cushion memory (commingled cap BY DESIGN; never recommend a per-client cap) concerns the shared share-balance cap and socialised loss; it is NOT contradicted here and no per-client cap is recommended. The issue is that an owner-chosen exit sequence moves the socialised loss off the cushion and onto the redeeming client. Contrast: totalWithdrawal (AYieldStrategy.sol:417 -> ERC4626MarketYieldStrategy._totalWithdraw :209-240) sells PRO-RATA shares (totalShares * clientBalance / totalDeposited) and does NOT shift the loss.
impact: No harm today: the strategy is not below par and the action has not been taken. If taken under a loss, V2 bears the minter's share of the loss (up to ~58% of the realised loss redistributed onto V2), realised as unbacked Antimatter/phUSD dilution.
attackPath: The commingled sUSDe position falls below par (V < D). This requires an sUSDe NAV decline (never observed historically; Ethena absorbs losses in its reserve fund), a prior emergencyWithdraw, or an M-05 (ryv18m5, formerly L-30) gapped-deposit-route strand. It CANNOT come from an sUSDe/USDe AMM discount: valuation uses convertToAssets and deposit crediting is haircut, so fairValueOfShares >= creditedPrincipal.
The owner, tidying up, calls withdrawAsOwner(OLD minter 0x435B, recipient, 3,749.62e18) on 0xaC2e…7f95.
_disposeShares sells convertToShares(3,749.62e18): the minter is paid full NAV of its principal.

Remaining backing per principal for V2 drops to (V - NAV(sold)) / (D - amount) < V/D; V2 holds the whole loss. (Mechanism is generic: any first exiter under V < D, V2 included, is paid full NAV; the owner-specific harm is that exiting the minter first reverses the intended cushion.)

recommendation: Operational (safe-config): withdraw the OLD minter's position only while the strategy's totalBalance >= principal (at or above par), or only after V2 has exited/migrated; or retire it with totalWithdrawal (pro-rata shares) rather than withdrawAsOwner. Document in the runbook / src/CLAUDE.md that withdrawAsOwner under a loss transfers the loss to the remaining clients.
safeConfigGuidance: Withdraw the OLD minter's position only at/above par, or after V2 has exited/migrated; prefer totalWithdrawal (pro-rata) over withdrawAsOwner when V < D.
escalationTrigger: MEDIUM if withdrawAsOwner (or any non-pro-rata exit) is executed for a non-redeeming minter client while the strategy is below par and V2 (or another redeeming client) remains in the position.
MEDIUM if a phStaging2 cleanup/cutover script schedules an OLD-minter withdrawAsOwner without an at-par precondition.
Re-weigh if a second REDEEMING client is authorized on the same strategy (the minter-cushion premise would fail).
